name: Hot spring
notes: Geothermal ground: colour-banded thermophile microbial mats in the runoff channels, heat-tolerant mosses and grasses on warm ground, and specialist wetland plants where the water cools. Drawn on Yellowstone, Iceland (Hveravellir, Reykjadalur), New Zealand (Rotorua) and Japanese onsen valleys.

canopy.name: Lodgepole pine
canopy.source: Pinus contorta, lodgepole pine, dominant tree ringing Yellowstone geyser basins (stunted near hot ground), 10-25 m — Wikipedia / NPS

canopy.name: Manuka
canopy.source: Leptospermum scoparium, manuka, dominant shrub-tree on warm geothermal ground at Rotorua/Taupo, NZ, 2-8 m — Wikipedia / NZ DOC

canopy.name: Downy birch
canopy.source: Betula pubescens, downy birch, scrub near Icelandic geothermal valleys, 3-10 m — Wikipedia

shrub.name: Prostrate kanuka
shrub.source: Kunzea ericoides, kanuka (prostrate geothermal form), on heated soils of NZ Taupo Volcanic Zone, 0.5-3 m — Wikipedia / NZ DOC

shrub.name: Geothermal willow
shrub.source: Salix lanata, woolly willow, dwarf willow on warm wet ground beside Icelandic hot springs, 0.3-1.5 m — Wikipedia

shrub.name: Shrubby cinquefoil
shrub.source: Dasiphora fruticosa, shrubby cinquefoil, common in wet meadows fringing Yellowstone thermal areas, 0.3-1.2 m — Wikipedia / USDA

shrub.name: Umbrella fern
shrub.source: Dicranopteris linearis, Old World forked fern, thicket-forming on heated ground in NZ and Asian geothermal fields, 0.5-2 m — Wikipedia / NZ DOC

ground.name: Thermophile mat
ground.source: Thermus aquaticus (with cyanobacteria Synechococcus/Phormidium), orange-red microbial mat in hot spring outflow channels at 50-80 C, Yellowstone/Iceland/NZ — Wikipedia / NPS

ground.name: Green cyanobacteria mat
ground.source: Synechococcus lividus, green thermophilic cyanobacterial mat in cooler (45-70 C) hot spring channels, Yellowstone — Wikipedia / NPS

ground.name: Hot-spring moss
ground.source: Bryum argenteum, silver moss, cosmopolitan moss on warm geothermal soil in Iceland/Yellowstone — Wikipedia

ground.name: Ross' bentgrass
ground.source: Agrostis rossiae, Ross' bentgrass, endemic annual grass growing only on heated ground in Yellowstone thermal areas, 5-20 cm — Wikipedia / NPS

ground.name: Geothermal kanuka moss
ground.source: Campylopus introflexus and geothermal moss carpets on hot soil at Rotorua, NZ, 1-5 cm — NZ DOC geothermal vegetation

ground.name: Tufted hairgrass
ground.source: Deschampsia cespitosa, tufted hairgrass, tussock of wet meadows around cooled hot spring outflows, Holarctic, 0.3-1.2 m — Wikipedia / USDA

ground.name: Broad-leaved cattail
ground.source: Typha latifolia, cattail, in warm outflow pools below hot springs, Holarctic, 1-3 m — Wikipedia
